To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression of ZIP‐1 and ZIP‐2 mRNA in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of asthmatic patients was higher than those of healthy subjects; 2) the expression of zinc transport mRNA in peripheral blood leukocytes of asthma patients was associated with the severity of asthma; 3) the expression of the zinc transporters ZIP‐1 and Zip‐2 mRNA were significantly higher in the leukocytes in the peripheral blood of asthma patients compared with healthy controls.
Overexpression of ZIP‐ 2 mRNA was found.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the zinc transporter ZIP‐2 in the development of asthma.
the role of zinc in the pathogenesis of asthma.
the expression of zinc transport genes in the leukocytes in asthmatic and healthy infants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zinc deficiency in asthmatic children may be a consequence, rather than a cause of asthma.
there is a strong relationship between zinc and asthma and that the role of zinc transporters in asthma should be further explored.
the zinc transporter ZIP2 gene is a potential asthma susceptibility gene, which may contribute to the increasing prevalence of asthma in the modern world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
zinc transporter ZIP‐2 is a candidate gene in asthma, and the overexpression of ZIP2 may play an important role in the pathogenesis of asthma.
the overexpression of ZIP 2 in the leukocytes may contribute to the development of asthma.
zinc is an essential trace element for normal human growth and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zinc deficiency in asthmatic patients may contribute to the pathophysiological process of asthma.
